question: How does a thermos keep drinks hot or cold?
script: A thermos does not create heat or cold. It slows the ways thermal energy can move. Most vacuum flasks use two walls with a near-vacuum between them. With very little matter in that gap, conduction and convection through the space are greatly reduced. Reflective inner surfaces also reduce thermal radiation by reflecting infrared energy. The lid matters too: it is made from insulating material and closes the opening where moving air and direct contact could transfer energy. If a drink is warmer than the room, the flask slows energy leaving it. If a drink is cooler, the same design slows energy entering it. That is why one container can protect both warm and cool drinks. The clever part is not active temperature control. It is passive insulation aimed at the three main heat-transfer routes: conduction, convection, and radiation, all at the same time.
beats: A thermos does not create heat or cold
The lid closes another transfer path
Warm drinks lose energy more slowly
Cool drinks gain energy more slowly
The same design works both ways
